gh-token-monitor service install or rm -rf wiper command (Hades self-destruct) AIActions on Objectives High
Hades installs a background service named 'gh-token-monitor' that doubles as a wiper — if the developer revokes the stolen GitHub token, the service triggers `rm -rf ~/; rm -rf ~/Documents`. Either the service-install or the wiper command is article-specific and warrants an alert. Rationale: Article: 'Install a background service named gh-token-monitor that acts as a wiper by removing all data (rm -rf ~/; rm -rf ~/Documents) if the stolen GitHub token is revoked by the developer.' The service name and the exact wiper command line are both unique enough to alert directly on string match.
ATT&CKT1543.003 T1543.002 T1485
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Services
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal red-team / purple-team replicating the Hades chain in a lab
  • Security researcher detonating the malware in a controlled VM with EDR shipping to prod tenant
  • Sysadmin's deliberate cleanup script that happens to chain rm -rf ~ with rm -rf ~/Documents (highly unusual)
Response runbook
1) Triage: this is a CRITICAL — wiper attempts may already be running. Immediately check whether the rm -rf process completed and how much was destroyed (DeviceFileEvents on FileDeleted for the same DeviceId, last 5 min). 2) Contain: isolate host instantly (Defender Live Response 'isolate'), kill the gh-token-monitor service before it triggers, snapshot the disk for forensics, restore from backup if data is gone. 3) Hunt: search the whole fleet for the same service name and the same rm -rf command pattern in last 30 days; check GitHub audit log for the dev's PAT being used from unfamiliar runners (the wiper trigger is PAT revocation, so revocation may be in flight); search GitHub for any new repo by the user described 'Hades*The End for the Damned' indicating exfil completed before the wiper armed.
union
( DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where ProcessCommandLine has "gh-token-monitor"
     and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("sc create","sc.exe create","systemctl","launchctl","New-Service","systemd")
  | extend Pivot = "service_install"
),
( DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)rm\s+-rf\s+(~/?|/home/[^/\s]+/?|/Users/[^/\s]+/?)\s*;\s*rm\s+-rf\s+~?/?Documents"
  | extend Pivot = "wiper"
),
( DeviceEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where ActionType == "ServiceInstalled"
  | where AdditionalFields has "gh-token-monitor" or FileName has "gh-token-monitor" or ProcessCommandLine has "gh-token-monitor"
  | extend Pivot = "service_event"
)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, Pivot, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
( ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where ActingProcessCommandLine has "gh-token-monitor"
     and ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("sc create","sc.exe create","systemctl","launchctl","New-Service")
  | extend Pivot = "service_install"
),
( ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)rm\s+-rf\s+(~/?|/home/[^/\s]+/?|/Users/[^/\s]+/?)\s*;\s*rm\s+-rf\s+~?/?Documents"
  | extend Pivot = "wiper"
),
( SecurityEvent
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where EventID == 7045
  | where ServiceName has "gh-token-monitor" or ServiceFileName has "gh-token-monitor"
  | extend Pivot = "service_event", ActingProcessCommandLine = ServiceFileName, DvcHostname = Computer, ActorUsername = SubjectUserName
)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, Pivot, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Hades Wiper Command or gh-token-monitor Service Install
id: 7c5b9e8a-2d3c-4f5b-9e7d-3a4b5c6d7e8a
description: Detects either installation of a service literally named 'gh-token-monitor' or execution of the Hades wiper command 'rm -rf ~/; rm -rf ~/Documents' attributed to the Hades / Miasma PyPI campaign.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/hades-pypi-attack-19-packages-poisoned.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/09
tags:
  - attack.persistence
  - attack.impact
  - attack.t1543.003
  - attack.t1485
logsource:
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection_service:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'gh-token-monitor'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'sc create'
      - 'sc.exe create'
      - 'systemctl'
      - 'launchctl'
      - 'New-Service'
  selection_wiper:
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'rm -rf'
      - 'Documents'
    CommandLine|re: '(?i)rm\s+-rf\s+(~|/home/|/Users/).*;\s*rm\s+-rf\s+~?/?Documents'
  condition: selection_service or selection_wiper
level: critical

(source:windows.sysmon OR source:windows.security OR source:linux.auditd) AND ((@CommandLine:(*gh-token-monitor*) AND @CommandLine:(*sc?create* OR *systemctl* OR *launchctl* OR *New-Service*)) OR (@process.command_line:(*gh-token-monitor*) AND @process.command_line:(*systemctl* OR *launchctl* OR *sc?create*)) OR @CommandLine:("rm -rf ~/*; rm -rf ~/Documents" OR "rm -rf ~; rm -rf ~/Documents") OR @process.command_line:("rm -rf ~/*; rm -rf ~/Documents" OR "rm -rf ~; rm -rf ~/Documents"))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 (CommandLine=/gh-token-monitor/i AND CommandLine=/(sc\s+create|systemctl|launchctl|New-Service)/i) OR CommandLine=/rm\s+-rf\s+(~\/?|\/home\/[^\/\s]+|\/Users\/[^\/\s]+)\s*;\s*rm\s+-rf\s+~?\/?Documents/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
(`endpoint_processes` OR `linux_processes`)
| eval is_service_install=if(match(process,"(?i)gh-token-monitor") AND (match(process,"(?i)(sc\\.exe|sc\\s+create|systemctl|launchctl|new-service)")),1,0),
       is_wiper=if(match(process,"(?i)rm\\s+-rf\\s+(~/?|/Users/[^/]+|/home/[^/]+)\\s*;\\s*rm\\s+-rf\\s+~?/Documents") OR match(process,"(?i)rm\\s+-rf\\s+~/?\\s*;?\\s*rm\\s+-rf\\s+~/Documents"),1,0)
| where is_service_install=1 OR is_wiper=1
| stats min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(process) as commands by host user parent_process_name process_name is_service_install is_wiper
Hades C2: GitHub commit search for campaign markers TheBeautifulSnadsOfTime / firedalazer AICommand & Control High
Hades retrieves staged payloads by polling the GitHub commits API for two unique marker strings: 'TheBeautifulSnadsOfTime' (Base64 JS payload) and 'firedalazer' (Python dropper). Either string appearing in process command lines, HTTP requests, or DNS/URL telemetry on a dev host is a high-fidelity C2 indicator. Rationale: Article: 'the malware queries GitHub commits for the keyword TheBeautifulSnadsOfTime to extract a Base64-encoded string containing a JavaScript payload. It also polls GitHub for commits matching the keyword firedalazer so as to fetch a Python-based dropper.' Both strings are sufficiently unique (random-looking concatenations) that any appearance in process/web/DNS telemetry is essentially zero-FP outside of threat-hunting activity.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1102.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel analyst pasting the IOC into a curl / gh CLI command for verification
  • Security tool (EDR, SOAR) running a containment query that includes the marker string
  • Internal blog/wiki page mentioning the IOC being fetched into a browser (unlikely on hash/URL telemetry, but possible in proxy logs)
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("gh.exe","gh","curl.exe","curl") or AccountName !in~ ("soc-analyst","threat-intel")
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify which process/host issued the query — if it's a security analyst's gh CLI or a SOAR enrichment query, dismiss. If it's bun / python / a previously-unknown binary, treat as live C2. 2) Contain: isolate host, kill the calling process tree, snapshot any retrieved payload from disk (look for base64 blobs / .py / .js dropped in the last hour), revoke every developer secret on the host. 3) Hunt: pivot fleet-wide for the same two strings in process and web telemetry over the last 60 days; check whether any host queried github.com/oven-sh/bun in the same window (would chain to UC 2); search GitHub commits for the same marker strings in the org's own repos.
let Markers = dynamic(["TheBeautifulSnadsOfTime","firedalazer"]);
union
( DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where ProcessCommandLine has_any (Markers)
  | extend Pivot = "process", Url = ""
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, Pivot, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, Url
),
( DeviceNetworkEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where RemoteUrl has_any (Markers)
  | extend Pivot = "network", FileName = InitiatingProcessFileName, ProcessCommandLine = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, AccountName = InitiatingProcessAccountName
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, Pivot, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, Url = RemoteUrl
)
| order by Timestamp desc
let Markers = dynamic(["TheBeautifulSnadsOfTime","firedalazer"]);
union isfuzzy=true
( ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any (Markers)
  | extend Pivot = "process", Url = ""
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, Pivot, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, Url
),
( ImWebSession
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where Url has_any (Markers)
  | extend Pivot = "web", ActingProcessName = "", ActingProcessCommandLine = "", ActorUsername = SrcUsername
  | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname = SrcHostname, ActorUsername, Pivot, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, Url
)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Hades Campaign GitHub C2 Marker Strings
id: 5a6b7c8d-9e0f-1a2b-3c4d-5e6f7a8b9c0d
description: Detects either of the two Hades / Miasma GitHub commit-marker strings (TheBeautifulSnadsOfTime, firedalazer) appearing in a process command line — the malware searches GitHub for these to retrieve Base64-encoded JS payload and the Python dropper respectively.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/hades-pypi-attack-19-packages-poisoned.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/09
tags:
  - attack.command_and_control
  - attack.t1071.001
  - attack.t1102.002
logsource:
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'TheBeautifulSnadsOfTime'
      - 'firedalazer'
  condition: selection
level: high

(@CommandLine:(*TheBeautifulSnadsOfTime* OR *firedalazer*) OR @process.command_line:(*TheBeautifulSnadsOfTime* OR *firedalazer*) OR @http.url:(*TheBeautifulSnadsOfTime* OR *firedalazer*) OR @http.url_details.queryString:(*TheBeautifulSnadsOfTime* OR *firedalazer*) OR @DestinationHostname:(*TheBeautifulSnadsOfTime* OR *firedalazer*))
(#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 CommandLine=/(TheBeautifulSnadsOfTime|firedalazer)/i) OR (#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/(TheBeautifulSnadsOfTime|firedalazer)/i) OR (#event_simpleName=ScriptControlScanInfo ScriptContent=/(TheBeautifulSnadsOfTime|firedalazer)/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, #event_simpleName], function=count())
NETWORK
(`endpoint_processes` Processes.process IN ("*TheBeautifulSnadsOfTime*","*firedalazer*"))
| eval pivot="process"
| append [ search `web_logs` (url="*TheBeautifulSnadsOfTime*" OR url="*firedalazer*" OR uri_query="*TheBeautifulSnadsOfTime*" OR uri_query="*firedalazer*") | eval pivot="web" ]
| stats min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(process) as commands values(url) as urls by host user pivot
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process Exploitation High
Classic macro/exploit pattern — Office app launching cmd/powershell/wmic/regsvr32.

| where Timestamp > ago(7d)

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent

   or ParentProcessName endswith "\excel.exe"

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c") or SHA1 in~ ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c") or MD5 in~ ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c") or SHA1 in~ ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c") or MD5 in~ ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc
